summary: V. W. Paranjpe (1887–1976) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Superintendent of the Publication Department at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, succeeding Shripad Krishna Belvalkar, and was attested as Professor Emeritus at Deccan College.
Vaibhav Singh is a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. He earned his PhD from the University of Reading in 2017, where he held a post attested in 2018.

Valaiyattur Venkayya (1864–1912) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He served as acting Government Epigraphist of Madras (~1903–1908), succeeding Eugen Hultzsch, and Acting Government Epigraphist for the Archaeological Survey of India (1905).

Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy who studied at Pennsylvania, Harvard, Tokyo, and Gakushuin. He taught at Harvard, Princeton, and other Japanese universities before serving as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1965–2002).
Valeria Gazizova is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her master's degree at the University of Oslo, where she studied under Hanna Havnevik and MA supervisor Per Kværne.

Valerie Hansen (born 1958) is a historian and sinologist who studied at Harvard and the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair. She held a post at East China Normal University and served as an associate professor and professor at Yale University.

Valerie Stoker is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who holds a post at Wright State University. She studied under traditional teachers D. Prahladachar and Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi.
Vamana was an Indologist who studied under traditional teachers Keshava, Dattatreya Sastri Nigudkar, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.
Vamanshastri Kinjawadekar was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under traditional teachers Dattatreya, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.

Van Austin Harvey (1926–2021) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Occidental, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale. He chaired programs at Southern Methodist and Pennsylvania, and was the George Edwin Burnell Professor of Religious Studies at Stanford (~1978–1996).
Vans Kennedy (1784–1846) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army (1817–1835) and as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1846).
Vasant Shinde is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who held posts as Professor and Professor of South Asian Archaeology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev (1881–1951) was a sinologist who studied at St. Petersburg University and under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1910–1951), the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1918–1951), and the National Library of Russia.

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev (1818–1900) was a sinologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kazan State University under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski. He served as professor at Kazan and Saint Petersburg State University, and was a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Vasily Radlov (1837–1918) was a linguist, historian, and archaeologist who studied at Berlin and Jena under Pott, Steinthal, and Schott. He directed the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and the Kunstkamera (1894–1918), and founded the Russian Museum of Ethnography.

Vasily Seseman (1884–1963) was a philosopher who studied at Saint Petersburg State University. He held academic posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1915–1918), Vytautas Magnus University (~1923–1940), and Vilnius University (~1940–1950).

Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale (1901–1991) was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn. He held professorships at Fergusson College and the University of Delhi, and taught at Visva-Bharati University.

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi (1893–1985) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Deccan College and Mumbai. He served as Principal of Morris College and Vidarbha Institute, and was Honorary Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at Nagpur University (1957–1966).

Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala (1904–1967) was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and Lucknow. He curated the Mathura Museum, directed the State Museum Lucknow, was Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India, and founded the Prakrit Text Society.

Vasudha Dalmia (born 1947) is an Indologist and historian educated at Miranda House, Cologne, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Heidelberg. She lectured at Tübingen and served as the Magistretti Distinguished Professor at UC Berkeley (2001–2012) and Tandon Professor at Yale (2013–2014).
